scenes.intro: That WURMPLE has crossed the same leaf twice. My notes say indecisive. My notes may be projecting.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: It chose a shady spot. We can observe without making it perform for us.
An unrecorded observation. Scandalous. I think I can survive one.
scenes.ending: Attendance: two people, one WURMPLE. Nothing discovered except a pleasant place to sit.

scenes.intro: Devon let me keep these discarded parts. A switch, a speaker, and an empty casing. None is connected to anything dangerous.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: A voice needs all three. My mother would add someone willing to listen. She repaired radios, not loneliness, but sometimes both improved.
The casing has her handwriting inside. Apparently sentimental significance is not an approved engineering category. It should be.
scenes.ending: I usually explain first and ask for help much later. Thank you for letting me try the reverse.

scenes.intro: The museum has boats. I have left my notebook closed. There is no assessment at the end of this outing.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I was hoping you might ask. I would like to try, if you would.
Company without a report is already something I wanted. I am glad we can say what we mean.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: We can keep learning about each other without turning it into a test.

scenes.intro: Peer review, outdoors. Our exercise is to notice three things without deciding we understand them completely.
questions: How would you like to respond?
A trainer walks past without stopping. Which observation can we actually support?
Last observation: one field scientist has stopped talking long enough to hear somebody else. Should that go in the report?
responses: A tree offers shelter without asking what the traveler intends to accomplish. An excellent working policy.
They may be waiting for someone. Or enjoying being alone. Observation does not grant permission to invent their feelings.
Precisely. A small fact, accurately described.
Precisely. Uncertainty deserves a place in the notes.
An improvement in method. Thank you for the very patient demonstration.
I asked for help, and listened to the answer. I would like to keep doing that.
scenes.ending: The third observation is mine: asking you made this better. I shall include that in the report.

scenes.intro: I wrote to my mother about the journey. Three pages on plants. One sentence on how much less alone I feel.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: Then I would like to write that we chose each other. Not that either of us stopped having a life of our own.
Then I shall write friend without surrounding it with just. It is a very substantial word.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep this annotated notebook. The margin says: leave room for another answer, and sometimes for lunch.

scenes.intro: One ordinary parcel. One short delivery. I have prepared my customer-service smile. Do not make eye contact with it.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Thanks. Nobody paid for express delivery. I keep having to remind my shoulders.
Halfway each? Revolutionary logistics. The parcel weighs less than my objection to asking.
scenes.ending: Delivered. Nothing exploded, nobody vanished, and I got to walk back with someone. A good working day.

scenes.intro: I know the destination. I do not know this street. There is a courier right there. We could perform the obscure ritual of asking.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Excuse us. Which way? There. A question, an answer, no permanent damage to my qualifications.
All right. I can ask for directions without explaining every mistake I have ever made first.
scenes.ending: The late delivery still happened. Today went better because I accepted help. Those facts do not cancel each other.

scenes.intro: No parcel. No deadline. I chose somewhere to go because I thought you might enjoy it. This is suspiciously difficult to invoice.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I would like that. Clear agreement, no reading between the shipping labels.
Good. I wanted your company. That was the point, not a hidden debt you were expected to repay.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: We can decide what this means ourselves. There is no form for it. I checked.

scenes.intro: Three stops, two sets of hands, nobody required to prove they can collapse heroically under a bag.
questions: How would you like to respond?
Second stop has a heavy parcel. The quickest route includes stairs. The longer route has a level path.
Third stop is closed for lunch. We can leave a clear note or agree a later time.
responses: A rest stop belongs in the plan before someone needs rescuing. I am writing that in unusually large letters.
We each take what we can carry, then meet. Trust involves letting someone out of your sight without assuming the worst.
A delivery plan with people still functioning at the end. Advanced stuff.
They asked for the level entrance. Good thing we consulted the person actually receiving it.
No mystery package in an inconvenient doorway. An unusually civilized conclusion.
A deadline discussed honestly is better than a heroic promise nobody asked for.
scenes.ending: Shared load. Better delivery. Mildly unbearable lesson in cooperation. I will recover.

scenes.intro: I used to make plans to repay a mistake. This one is because I want there to be another journey after this one.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: Me too. We can keep our own destinations and decide together when the road is shared.
Then keep a place for me on the next route. Friend is not a lower class of delivery.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: This route card has a space marked rest. Use it. That instruction is also addressed to me.

scenes.intro: This is a practice performance. Very small. WHISMUR has agreed to be the audience. It has not agreed to be a small audience.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Thank you. That was enough applause, WHISMUR. You can stop applauding the bench now.
I can manage the first note if somebody else is here when it happens.
scenes.ending: One song. No audition panel appeared out of the shrubbery. A promising beginning.

scenes.intro: My uncle kept a place open at an audition. I never arrived. For a while I could not look at a noticeboard without reading it as an accusation.
questions: How would you like to respond?
options: Ask what he wants to play
responses: One piece, a familiar place, and permission to leave afterward. That sounds like a plan made for a person.
The walking song. I know it well enough that I can hear it even when my hands forget.
scenes.ending: I can write to him without attaching a success story. I think he wanted news of me.

scenes.intro: This piece has the rhythm of our footsteps. Yours are less predictable than mine. I mean that as a compliment. I think.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I would like it to mean a date, if you want that too. The music should not have to ask on my behalf.
I would be proud to call it that. Friendship can have a dedication. The paper is not exclusively reserved.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: I will write the name you agree to. Not the one I hoped you would guess.

scenes.intro: One song is enough. I am saying it before I invent twelve impossible conditions for allowing myself to start.
questions: How would you like to respond?
The middle phrase goes wrong. There is still a room, a song, and a perfectly serviceable next note.
The song ends. Somebody asks for another. I wanted to play one today.
responses: There. The first note was not perfect. It did successfully become the second note.
Thank you. A performance can be a shared room rather than a cliff with people below it.
The next note arrived. It did not demand a written apology for the last one.
A breath belongs in music. I am allowed one even if it was not printed there.
One was the plan. I can be pleased they listened without owing them the rest of the evening.
Another day sounds possible. I can look forward to it without promising tonight.
scenes.ending: I played because I wanted to. Not because being frightened had finally stopped. I am keeping that distinction.

scenes.intro: An encore, by choice. I still get nervous. I also look forward to seeing who will be listening.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I want that too. We can be close without making every song a declaration or every quiet day a problem.
Then I will keep a seat for you, and leave you free to choose it. That feels like a good tradition.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: This is the footsteps score. There is a rest in it. It means rest, not that somebody has gone away.

scenes.intro: A picnic with one spare chair. Grandmother insisted on it. The chair was more sociable than several paying customers.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: A seat before a sales pitch. Good. People should not have to explain why they look tired.
There. An invitation with no obligation attached. Also a sandwich with structural ambitions.
scenes.ending: Someone sat for five minutes and left smiling. I am counting that as excellent attendance.

scenes.intro: Two batches. One imitates grandmother perfectly until you taste it. The other tastes like something I actually made on purpose.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: More berry, less trying to win an argument with a memory. It turns out those are different ingredients.
She liked the crust dark. I like it soft. I spent a year treating that as a moral disagreement.
scenes.ending: I can love her cooking without turning my kitchen into a museum with burnt toast.

scenes.intro: Two seats reserved. I checked the chair stability twice. I would like to clarify the part of this meal that is not carpentry.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I hoped so. Let us say it properly before I attempt to communicate through suspiciously shaped bread.
Then a very good meal with a very good friend. No disappointing menu substitution involved.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: The food can be a surprise. What we mean to each other should not have to be.

scenes.intro: Our imaginary customer wants something soft, not too sweet, with no berries. We have supplied flour, milk, and a remarkable quantity of opinions.
questions: How would you like to respond?
One customer wants the filling separate. Our sample supplies include two little plates. An extravagant technological solution.
Last customer just wants somewhere to sit. They have brought their own lunch.
responses: Excellent. We have listened to the person instead of preparing my most impressive unrelated pastry.
Yes. Asking what someone enjoys is not a failure of artistic vision. My apron has been informed.
Problem solved without a speech about how the recipe was intended to be enjoyed.
A smaller portion, they say. Good. I am serving a person, not defending a blueprint.
A spare chair finally encountering its natural purpose. Grandmother would approve.
Water, no charge. Not every kind thing needs to become a new product.
scenes.ending: A kitchen that listens. I think that is the sort I want to run.

scenes.intro: A cafe plan. The spare chair stays. The address is still blank; I want to see a little more of the world before choosing a door.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: Yes. Room for us, and room for journeys neither of us has thought of yet.
The first invitation is yours. No expiry date. You do not have to earn your seat by arriving hungry.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep the recipe card. It includes an instruction to make room. That part is not about the dough.

scenes.intro: A small card trick. Everyone knows it is a trick. The extraordinary bow, however, is performed entirely without assistance.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Only if you want to join in. Nobody has been selected by an ominous destiny or by me pointing very loudly.
You choose a card; I attempt to be impressive. If I fail, the card remains a card and I remain overdressed.
scenes.ending: A willing audience and one extremely excessive bow. Honest work, at last.

scenes.intro: I told my old friend the truth. It did not produce instant forgiveness. My career in dramatic shortcuts suffered a serious setback.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Apologies, changed behavior, and time they were free to spend elsewhere. None could be replaced by a better speech.
Thank you. You are not here to take their place or declare the matter settled. I needed to learn that too.
scenes.ending: A reveal can finish a trick. Repairing trust has rather less convenient timing.

scenes.intro: No misdirection. No mysterious invitation on a velvet card. Would you like this outing to be a date?
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Then yes means yes because you said it. A simple method. I am scandalized that I did not adopt it sooner.
Then friends. A sincere invitation does not become a trap when the answer changes the plan.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: There. Plainly asked, plainly answered. I may need a small theatrical bow to recover.

scenes.intro: An openly explained routine. We arrange the cards together. Nobody is tricked into volunteering, and the secret is not used to embarrass anyone.
questions: How would you like to respond?
Second part: a volunteer wants to know where to stand. We can mark the spot or walk through it together.
Last part: somebody declines to volunteer. A lesser magician might insist they are secretly delighted.
responses: A puzzle offered honestly can still be delightful. The false emergency has been removed from the program.
A willing audience changes the entire room. Wonder does not become less valuable when everyone can leave.
A visible mark. The audience is allowed to know where the stage ends.
No surprise pull, no theatrical shove. The routine has mysteriously lost its most stressful feature.
An answer honored without turning it into another act. I find I prefer this version of myself.
A trick with no unwilling participant. The pigeons will have to generate their own publicity.
scenes.ending: Resolve, no hidden cards. It is an excellent title. I shall resist making it six words longer.

scenes.intro: An ordinary outing. I bought the refreshments normally. No dove brought the receipt. I find myself rather happy about this.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I would like that. A mutual choice, renewed by how we treat each other, not maintained by a clever performance.
Then I choose that too. A good friend does not need to be dazzled into staying.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep this signed trick card. It says: ask honestly. The signature is genuine. The flourish is regrettable.

scenes.intro: My first moon poem was about that sort of streetlamp. I defended the astronomy for weeks. The lamp declined to comment.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: It was extremely sincere and contained four uses of silver. My aunt kept it anyway. That was the part I did not understand then.
Thank you. I occasionally become sincere if nobody startles me with a compliment.
scenes.ending: You can remember the terrible moon. Please also remember somebody bothered to read it.

scenes.intro: Three draft endings. One is clever, one is cruel, and one says what I meant. Naturally I hid the third under the others.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: It says I wanted someone to stay. Astonishingly poor camouflage. My aunt would have put it on the good shelf.
You listened to the ugly drafts too. I thought being taken seriously required arriving already finished.
scenes.ending: I kept the honest one. You may witness my artistic downfall into meaning things.

scenes.intro: I wrote this while we traveled. No ironic footnote. I would like you to hear it before I regain my defensive punctuation.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Yes, that was in the poem. I could have simply asked. Apparently I needed weather imagery first.
Then I am glad it is a friendship poem. Those deserve better endings than an embarrassed apology.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: We can be clear about this. I refuse to let an unattended metaphor make our decisions.

scenes.intro: Three people agreed to hear a reading outside the tent. Three actual people, with ears. There goes my anonymous reputation.
questions: How would you like to respond?
Second verse. I can rush through the important line or pause long enough for them to hear it.
Someone asks which line matters most. I have prepared a distracting anecdote about punctuation.
responses: A small honest verse is enough. I do not need to become somebody louder to be heard.
An excellent opening disaster. Now I can admit the new poem matters without pretending I have never been ridiculous.
There. A silence that belongs to the poem, rather than a joke hastily pushed in front of it.
My pace. That is allowed. I keep expecting poetry to come with a minimum speed limit.
The line about wanting company. Yes. I have now said it without an obscuring weather system.
I want to say what I wrote. The anecdote can remain in protective custody.
scenes.ending: I read it anyway. My hands shook. The poem survived. Both observations can be true.

scenes.intro: This travel journal has blank pages. Formerly a terrifying design flaw. I think I understand them better now.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I want that too. We can make room for separate poems and still choose the same table.
Yes. A continuing friendship, with room for your life and mine. No consolation-prize stationery.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep the handwritten poem. It ends with an open window. I am allowing some fresh air into the symbolism.

scenes.intro: Presenting the folding rest seat. Its first consultant gets to sit down. An audacious break with the tradition of testing things on unwilling friends.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Locked, tested, and nobody underneath it while I demonstrate. My reputation for excitement has limits.
Somebody who needs a rest. They do not need a diagnosis or a persuasive speech to qualify.
scenes.ending: POKEMON included only if they want to. ELECTRIKE has requested a cushion. Negotiations are progressing.

scenes.intro: Three sketches. A very fast tool, a very loud tool, and a simple grip someone can use without hurting their hand.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Dad would ask what problem it solves. For once I can answer before describing the motor.
We should have started there. Accessibility designed without asking people is often just an attractive new obstacle.
scenes.ending: I still like spectacular inventions. I would like people to enjoy using them too.

scenes.intro: No prototypes today. The bag contains lunch, a blanket, and no component I can describe as experimental.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Yes, please. Actual date. No surprise product-testing waiver included.
Absolutely. I can want company without trying to upgrade it into something else.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: A walk can be the entire plan. This is deeply inconvenient news for my emergency planning notebook.

scenes.intro: A disconnected demonstration circuit. No live current. ELECTRIKE has chosen to watch from over there, which is a complete and valid job.
questions: How would you like to respond?
Second check: the handle is hard to grip. We can make it larger or offer a different shape.
Last check: someone says they do not want to try it today. The device is ready. What next?
responses: The damaged wire gets replaced, not hidden under enthusiasm. We can be excited after the safety check.
Agreed. Consent is not an obstacle between me and a successful demonstration. It is part of one.
That gives more room to hold it. We test with the person using it, not with my triumphant expression.
Different hands, different solutions. One universal grip was a very optimistic label.
Stopped. No injury to the device, and no requirement that somebody justify saying no.
Only if they want. The test schedule is not more important than the person.
scenes.ending: Trust before voltage. I should put that on the toolbox where I cannot claim not to have seen it.

scenes.intro: The rest-stop proposal has a wide entrance and more than one kind of seat. It also has a budget. I have made peace with two of those facts.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I would like that. You are a person I choose, not a project I am going to finish.
Yes. A friendship with room to move, and permission to tell me when the machine is too loud.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep this blueprint. The most important measurement says: ask the person who will use it.

scenes.intro: An ominous noise. A mysterious shadow. A portable hinge in need of oil. We may be witnessing the least demanding haunting in local history.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: A squeak. No ghost required. We may still tell a good story about the hinge.
An excellent pause. Not knowing yet is more honest than announcing a very marketable curse.
scenes.ending: Grandmother charged this sort of ghost rent. I suspect the ghost would have asked for maintenance.

scenes.intro: Two neighbors remembered different endings to her story. I almost corrected one. Then I realized whose voice I was about to lose.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Two versions, with their names beside them. A memory can be precious without becoming the only permitted account.
One remembered a warning. One remembered a joke. She made room for both sorts of person.
scenes.ending: I do not have to recover every word to keep something kind alive.

scenes.intro: You appear in my travel story. I would prefer to ask how you want to be described instead of quietly assigning you a fate.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I would like to explore that too. A story should not turn a hope into a promise someone never made.
Then friend belongs on the page. A very old and durable sort of magic, if we are speaking poetically.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: We can leave the uncertain parts open. Paper is surprisingly patient when you stop threatening it with an ending.

scenes.intro: This tale blames an absent traveler for a broken gate. Nobody asked the traveler. The gate appears to have been broken long before the arrival.
questions: How would you like to respond?
The second account says a neighbor repaired the gate. The old tale never mentions that work.
The final line can blame a stranger or remember how the village helped. Both fit on the page.
responses: The traveler, and the person who repaired it. A convenient villain can hide an astonishing amount of ordinary work.
The village fixes its gate together. Less dramatic, perhaps. Considerably more useful to the next traveler.
A name returned to the story. Sometimes that changes more than a dramatic new ending.
Ordinary skill, generously used. It deserves at least as much space as the invented curse.
A village with neighbors instead of a convenient villain. A considerable improvement in its prospects.
Yes. Someone else may know a detail we have not heard. The page need not pretend to be the last word.
scenes.ending: I can love an old tale and still refuse the part that treats somebody unfairly.

scenes.intro: I wrote an ordinary entry. We walked, we ate, you waited while I found a word. Nobody saved the world before lunch.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I want that too. Love can join a life without being asked to replace everyone who is gone.
Yes. A friend who remembers kindly is not a lesser ending. I hope the next pages have room for both our names.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep this booklet. Some stories have two endings. This one is allowed to continue.

scenes.intro: The pocket inspection. One lunch parcel, one travel pouch, and a stern warning from the sandwich about decorative storage.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: It sits without pulling. A promising development in the radical field of clothes people can actually wear.
Secure, but not so stiff that opening lunch becomes an athletic achievement. We are making progress.
scenes.ending: The sandwich has approved the trial. Its written review is several crumbs.

scenes.intro: I won a prize for an outfit that looked like somebody else had made it. Everybody congratulated me. I went home and could not draw.
questions: How would you like to respond?
options: Ask what she wants to make
responses: Something that lets people feel like themselves. It sounds obvious until applause starts offering very specific instructions.
The pockets work. The person can sit. I can see my own choices on the page. I missed that.
scenes.ending: A prize can be pleasant without being the only trustworthy opinion in the room.

scenes.intro: I made this sketch with you in mind. Not a demand to wear anything. More a fairly well-dressed invitation.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: I hoped it could be. We can agree about that without agreeing on every color combination.
Then it is a friendship sketch, with the same excellent pockets. Practical affection is not reserved for couples.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: You get to choose what feels right. I am remarkably consistent about that, for someone carrying this many fabric samples.

scenes.intro: A packing challenge. Lunch, map, repair kit. All supplied. There is no secret correct answer in which somebody forgets to eat.
questions: How would you like to respond?
Next: the repair kit has a sharp needle. There is a closed inner pocket and a small supplied case.
Last: the map needs to stay dry. A flap or the supplied wrapping will work.
responses: Yes. Frequently needed things within reach. I am refusing the theory that inconvenience proves elegance.
Comfort and access, together. There is more than one successful arrangement. The bag is not grading your personality.
Protected and easy to identify. Nobody should discover sewing equipment by sitting on it.
A sensible case. Decorative suffering has once again failed to improve the outfit.
Secure. We can find the route without first drying an entire coastline.
Good. The map has survived lunch and weather. More than one arrangement can be a successful design.
scenes.ending: Room for lunch, and room for the person carrying it. An ambitious design philosophy.

scenes.intro: Finished sketch. Working pockets. Space for things you care about, including the things I would not have thought to pack.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I want that too. We can choose each other without tailoring either person into someone smaller.
Then this is a very good traveling friendship. No alterations required to make it count.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep the sketch. The angry sandwich has signed the corner. I am choosing to call that professional recognition.

scenes.intro: Portable practice board. Permission obtained. Three colors, one bird shaped like a bent spoon. The bird has seniority.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Good. A sky that looks like someone left the door open for the sun. My brother would demand an even bigger brush.
It is how I drew them when we painted together. I can improve without evicting every ridiculous old friend.
scenes.ending: A small board is enough for a beginning. It does not have to become a permanent monument to deserve care.

scenes.intro: Three neighbors shared what they wanted remembered: a garden, a meeting place, and somebody who always brought an extra chair.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: Different opinions fit beside each other. A community is inconveniently larger than my first composition.
Yes. Being willing to talk is not the same as agreeing to become a public portrait.
scenes.ending: I have their permission for a small panel. No borrowed wall, no claim to have spoken for everybody.

scenes.intro: You have a place in the sketch if you want one. I would also like your company somewhere without a paint tin between us.
questions: How would you like to respond?
responses: That is what I hoped. Thank you for asking directly before I attempted to communicate through composition.
Then company it is. You are already important to me; I do not need a romantic label to prove it.
There is no deadline. We can enjoy today and talk again when you want to.
scenes.ending: We choose what this is together. I can leave some space without being frightened of the blank part.

scenes.intro: The old wall is gone. This panel will not replace it, or the people in that memory. It can carry something they helped make.
questions: How would you like to respond?
The panel can include the garden and the meeting place without painting a neighbor who declined a portrait.
Last detail: somebody offers another memory. There is still a little room around the border.
responses: The enormous sky, then. And one terrible bird. A detail can hold a memory without pretending to preserve everything.
Yes. Keeping something does not mean refusing everything that comes afterward.
A garden bench, then. A place can suggest a welcome without borrowing somebody who said no.
Their decision stays theirs. Empty space is not an artistic emergency.
A few words in their own voice. The picture is better for making room.
A second panel, with permission again. Finishing one work does not require declaring the community complete.
scenes.ending: More than a wall. People remembered, permission respected, a story allowed to change hands.

scenes.intro: This travel mural has more people than the first sketch. Everyone who helped gets a little space. The birds remain catastrophically aerodynamic.
questions: Only one committed romance at a time. What do you both want?
responses: I would like that. With room for our friends, our work, and whichever road makes sense next.
Yes. A lasting friendship belongs in the picture. Nobody is being painted out to make the ending tidier.
We can take more time. The invitation will still be here.
scenes.ending: Keep this print. It includes you as you chose to appear. There is room around the edges for another journey.

gift_replies.silas: A useful field supply. Thank you. I have recorded the gift without subjecting it to peer review.
gift_replies.kade: Thanks. I will actually use this. That is an endorsement, despite my face doing its usual thing.
gift_replies.ashe: Thank you. I had a longer thank-you prepared. That one was the important part.
gift_replies.nico: Lovely. I promise not to describe anything in the first-aid kit as a mystery ingredient.
gift_replies.riven: A genuine gift! Received with gratitude, and with no secret compartment involved.
gift_replies.emi: Thank you. I accept thoughtful supplies as well as compliments. Slightly less evasively, in fact.
gift_replies.vera: Thank you! Useful, portable, and apparently not in need of an experimental motor. Excellent.
gift_replies.lume: Thank you. I shall keep it somewhere practical. A mysterious cupboard adds very little to a travel supply.
gift_replies.mochi: Thank you! A useful thing, with a sensible place to keep it. A surprisingly strong combination.
gift_replies.zuri: Thank you. Supplies matter. The less glamorous corner of a project is still part of the picture.
